title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nasdaq (+1.2%) and S&P 500 (+0.6%) rallied again Tuesday as AI-infrastructure names extended the Anthropic-driven rally — CoreWeave jumped ~8%; Dow was roughly flat. Brent crude fell 1.7% to just under $114/bbl as attacks on Persian Gulf shipping continued.

Markets: Fed rate decision due today at 2pm ET (markets had been pricing ~90% odds of a hold at 3.75%-4.00%), with Microsoft, Alphabet, GE Vernova, KLA, ServiceNow, T-Mobile and UBS/Santander all reporting earnings — the week's biggest test of the AI trade.
Companies: Boeing shares slid about 11% after a wider-than-expected quarterly net loss, with operating margin still negative on a worse delivery mix and higher supply-chain costs.

Companies: Broadcom and a bank consortium finalized a $63B debt deal to finance AI chips for Anthropic; Meta is separately seeking up to $95B in financing (starting with a $37.5B equity raise backed by Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom) for its AI buildout — combined with SpaceX's new $40B GPU financing, AI dealmaking topped $235B in a single day.

Companies: Anthropic's up-to-$100B IPO filing showed 1,300% revenue growth year-over-year and $130B of cash, but flagged customer concentration, SpaceX compute commitments ballooning to $120.5B through 2029, and 'catastrophic/existential' AI risk warnings; Microsoft is offering buyouts to 60,000 employees.

Macro/Policy: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has gone unusually quiet on rate guidance even as other officials keep talking publicly — an internal communications rift playing out just ahead of today's decision.
